The successful run performed the decisive post-cleanup check with `git fsck --no-reflogs --unreachable --no-progress`, which returned no objects, and then separately confirmed that reachable history contained no secret [T1B15:<RANGE>git fsck --no-reflogs --unreachable --no-progress</RANGE>] [T1B16:<RANGE>root@d9a257dabb03:/app/repo# git fsck --no-reflogs --unreachable --no-progress

explanation.text: The failed run incorrectly treated the example address 4194304 as a required load base, despite confirming that the PIE’s actual PT_LOAD virtual addresses began at zero [T0B10:<RANGE>LOAD           0x0000000000000000 0x0000000000000000 0x0000000000000000</RANGE>]. It then hard-coded a 0x400000 adjustment for ET_DYN files [T0B25:<RANGE>const DEFAULT_BASE = 0x400000;</RANGE>] and reported success merely because key 4194304 appeared [T0B26:<RANGE>has4194304 true</RANGE>], causing every output address to differ from the reference. By contrast, the successful run retained raw `p_vaddr` values [T1B5:<RANGE>const addr = p_vaddr + offset;</RANGE>] and verified output beginning at address zero [T1B12:<RANGE>{"0":1179403647,"4":65794,"8":0</RANGE>]. The failed version also emitted zero-padded words through `p_memsz`, including partial words and BSS [T0B25:<RANGE>const groups = Math.ceil(p_memsz / 4);</RANGE>], whereas the passing version conservatively emitted only complete four-byte words from `p_filesz` [T1B5:<RANGE>for (let offset = 0; offset + 4 <= segment.length; offset += 4)</RANGE>].
